trajectory_summary: This is a short, mechanical verify-and-DQ call: the rep runs through address, title, utility, bill, and roof questions efficiently, then hits a hard credit-score gate the customer cannot currently clear. The rep accepts the stated credit answer at face value, asks one generic follow-up, and closes the call with no callback plan or next step. Energy never built because the rep didn't probe the return-lead history or the co-owner angle before disengaging.
outcome_dispute: The customer discloses at 01:57 that they contacted Ion before ('I did reach out to you guys couple couple months back') and were told to come back once credit clears 670 — this is a recycled/returning lead, not a fresh one, and the rep never surfaces or logs this fact for follow-up. Given qualifiers.credit_qualifier's unresolved policy question (stated vs. pulled credit), a dq tag is defensible only if setter-level stated-credit DQ is confirmed as Ion's actual policy; if the closer's pull is meant to be the real gate, this call is a lost deal, not a clean DQ.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The customer's self-reported credit score falls below Ion's stated 670 threshold and the call ends without an appointment or callback plan; per qualifiers.credit_qualifier this is a hard_dq per current schema, though the underlying stated-vs-pulled-credit policy question (see spencer_operator_note) means this DQ should be reconciled with Kenny before treating it as unambiguously correct procedure.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the bill figure and simply repeated it back numerically ('That's 2 to 300') without acknowledging the pain language the customer used moments earlier ('getting up there pretty high') or tying it forward to a reason to act; the call moved directly to roof type instead.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The call ended at the credit disqualification before the rep reached the bill-collection stage of the script; the physical utility bill was never raised.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar; the call moved directly from the intro into address/title/utility/bill/roof verify questions and then hit the credit DQ before any interest question was raised.

script_coverage.quote: Hey. This is Bucky with ION reaching out about the solar form you filled online. How you doing?
Is it are you at 31 Woodland Hills Road?
Okay. Anybody else in the title but you?
Do you know what kind of roof you have? Is it a shingle?
What utility company are you with?
do you know how much you're spending on a monthly average?
do you have a credit score over 670?
Okay. Well, then no problem. You can always reach out anytime, and you have a great day.

attempt_quotes: Okay. Do do you know anybody that does or that could help?
objections.reasoning: This is a hard qualifier gate rather than a persuadable objection, so a single follow-up attempt is a defensible floor — but it is not a strong attempt: it doesn't probe the co-owner (wife) credit angle that was already on the table, so it should not be read as exhausting the available options.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Okay. Do do you know anybody that does or that could help?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The wife was already identified as a co-owner at 00:39; when the customer's own credit disqualified him, the rep had a live, schema-grounded option (spouse's credit) sitting right there and didn't use it. This is a concrete, replayable miss distinct from the general policy question about stated-vs-pulled credit.

key_moments.quote: do you have a credit score over 670?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier exactly per script phrasing, and the customer immediately self-reports below threshold. Per qualifiers.credit_qualifier's spencer_operator_note, stated credit and pulled credit often diverge by 30-50 points across bureaus, so a customer self-reporting sub-670 may still qualify on the bureau Ion actually pulls.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. So our credit kinda got hit a little bit recently.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers that this is a repeat contact with Ion ('I did reach out to you guys couple couple months back') and that a prior rep gave them the 670 threshold. The rep never asks when they last spoke to Ion, who told them this, or logs the return-lead status for follow-up.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Do do you know anybody that does or that could help?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer already disclosed at 00:39 that his wife is also on the title. When credit disqualifies the customer individually, the rep's generic 'know anybody that could help' line misses the concrete, schema-relevant angle of asking whether the co-owner's credit could qualify the household instead.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Well, then no problem. You can always reach out anytime, and you have a great day.
key_moments.stewart_read: No callback date, no timeframe, no 'reach back out in X months once your credit clears' — the exit is entirely passive and puts 100% of the burden on the customer to re-initiate.
